cases.sentence: Я и ___, потомок Авраама из рода Вениамина.
cases.explain: «сам израильтянин» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

cases.sentence: Но их падение принесло спасение язычникам, которое должно возбудить ревность и в ___.
cases.explain: «самих израильтянах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

cases.explain: «отдельные ветви» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree,

cases.sentence: Ведь если Бог не пожалел ___, то Он не пожалеет и тебя.
cases.explain: «природных ветвей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: for if God didn’t spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

cases.sentence: Если ты был срезан с дикого по природе ___ и вопреки своей природе был привит к окультуренному дереву, то тем более природные ветви привьются к своему собственному дереву!
cases.explain: «масличного дерева» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

cases.sentence: Если ты был срезан с дикого по природе масличного дерева и вопреки своей природе был привит к окультуренному дереву, то тем более ___ привьются к своему собственному дереву!
cases.explain: «природные ветви» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

cases.translation: For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?
